company_name: China International Marine Containers (Group) Co., Ltd. (CIMC)

inputs.share_count_basis: 5,392.5M issued (A+H) less 165.0M treasury shares held at 30 Jun 2026 (79.98M H shares from the 2025 H-share repurchases + 85.06M A shares from the 2023/2025 A-share repurchases; H1-2026 interim, Chapter VI). Treasury shares carry no dividend/voting rights and are held for cancellation/ESOP within three years. No convertibles; employee schemes are immaterial. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and buybacks are value-neutral.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual, CF supplementary note V.67: share-based payment expense was a net REVERSAL of RMB85.4m (forfeited awards); treated as 0, not as a credit. H1-2026 charge RMB11.3m (0.014% of revenue); FY2023 RMB88.7m (0.07%). Forward path held at 0.05% of revenue. No equity-award tax line disclosed (PRC filer).
inputs.buyback_note: RMB913m repurchased in FY2025 (H shares HK$452m + A shares RMB498m) plus HK$173m of H shares in H1-2026; HK$173m second-batch remainder approved Jul-2026, not yet implemented at 28 Aug 2026. Repurchased shares are held in treasury (deducted from the count above), not cancelled.
inputs.fx_note: Statements in RMB (CASBE, RMB'000 rescaled to millions); H-share quote in HKD. fx_rate = HKD per CNY = 1.1724 (Yahoo Finance CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-16 22:02Z). Direction/parity check against the Shenzhen A-share 000039.SZ (CNY 8.02 at 2026-10-16 close): the H-share price divided by 1.1724 implies a ~38% A-over-H premium, consistent with CIMC's historical 30-60% AH premium; a reversed rate would imply a near-zero premium. All values are built in CNY and converted to HKD at this rate; refresh_price.py does not move fx_rate, so re-date it on the next full rebuild.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY: risk-free 1.9% (10y China government bond), ERP 7.0% (mature ERP plus China country premium), beta 1.25 for a cyclical capital-goods conglomerate -> cost of equity ~11%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~3.5% (RMB/USD bank debt and debentures; FY2025 interest expense RMB1.51bn on ~RMB34-41bn debt) -> ~2.6% after tax. Weights ~70/30 equity/debt at market (H-basis equity ~CNY30bn vs net debt + perpetuals ~CNY17bn; the A-share basis would raise the equity weight). WACC 8.5%, identical across scenarios: cyclicality, US trailer duties and SOE governance are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not as a rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A) leases as debt: lease liabilities (RMB1,039.9m, 30 Jun 2026) deducted once in the equity bridge; lease principal NOT deducted from flows; right-of-use renewals (~RMB0.6bn/yr of new ROU assets) charged through the capex path (+~0.35pp of revenue). total_debt excludes leases.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated (CIMC Vehicles ~61%, Enric ~70%, Raffles ~83%, TianDa ~66%, Wetrans ~63% owned); minority interests deducted ONCE in the bridge at book (RMB17,166m, 30 Jun 2026). Book NCI is ~27% of book equity ex-perpetuals, close to a mid-cycle NCI profit share of ~25-30% (FY2018-24 ex-FY2023); FY2025/H1-26 NCI shares of 83%/46% reflect parent-level container/FX/finance losses at a trough and are not used as the run-rate.
inputs.perpetual_bond_treatment: Perpetual bonds (RMB4,016m 'other equity instruments', 30 Jun 2026) are included in core_metrics shareholders' equity and net income; they are a senior claim on ordinary holders and are deducted in the bridge as debt.
inputs.ebitda_definition: Underlying EBITDA = gross profit - taxes & surcharges - selling - G&A - R&D + other income + D&A (fixed-asset depreciation + ROU depreciation + intangible and long-term-prepaid amortisation from the CF supplementary note). Excludes investment income/associates (their asset is in the bridge), fair-value moves, FX/financial expenses and disposal gains. History (pre-impairment): FY2019 ~7.3%, FY2020 ~8.6%, FY2021 13.5% (container boom), FY2022 9.3%, FY2023 7.4%, FY2024 7.8%, FY2025 7.8%, H1-2026 ~7.0%. Average ex-FY2021 ~8.0%. The driver paths are stated NET of recurring asset + credit impairments (~0.5-0.9% of revenue: FY2024 0.5%, FY2025 0.9%, H1-2026 0.35%), so the mid-cycle ~8.0% gross maps to ~7.5% in the base path.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component build) with the non-US/cyclical adaptations, per dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials'. CIMC is a capital-equipment manufacturer (containers, trailers, energy/chemical equipment, offshore engineering) with a small finance/leasing arm whose debt sits in consolidated net debt; it is not a bank or holdco, so owner FCF is the right flow. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). CYCLICAL NORMALISATION: the reported FCF base is not used as a run-rate. FY2025 reported FCF of RMB13.8bn included a ~RMB7.8bn working-capital release (receivables -6.5bn, inventories -0.9bn) that reversed in H1-2026 (FCF -2.3bn); TTM to Jun-26 is ~RMB6.4bn. The forward flows are built from a mid-cycle underlying EBITDA margin (see ebitda_definition), D&A 2.8%, capex ~3.0% incl. ROU renewals, cash tax normalising toward 26-28% on unlevered EBIT (FY2024-25 book ETR was 36-52% because loss-making parent/finance entities shelter nothing), and working capital at -8% of incremental revenue (net operating working capital ~7% of revenue: receivables + inventory + contract assets exceed payables + contract liabilities). Interest income is not deducted from last_fcf because the company is net-debt and the EBITDA build already excludes financial income/expense. Net debt RMB13,013m at 30 Jun 2026 = borrowings + current portion of non-current liabilities + debentures (34,191.9) less cash at bank and on hand (21,178.6); year-end net debt is seasonally lower (FY2025 10,084). Horizon 10 years so the recovery to mid-cycle is complete before capitalising; terminal cap 12x (cyclical), WACC 8.5% all scenarios.
inputs.band_note: House and street bases nearly coincide: SBC is ~0.01-0.07% of revenue (PRC filer; FY2025 a net reversal), so the house/street band is ~HKD0.3 wide and the generated band_position is degenerate (price lies below both ends). Read this as an SBC-zero market: the band collapsed and band_position carries no information.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR 2.7% vs revenue 5y CAGR 10.7% and EPS 5y CAGR -49.8% (FY2020 EPS rebased for the FY2022 10-for-5 bonus issue: 1.41 x 3,595/5,392.5 = 0.94). All three end-points sit at different points of the container cycle; none is a forward growth estimate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (interest income not deducted: net-debt company). FY2025 owner FCF 13,795.7 (SBC reversal treated as 0); FY2022 10,527.1; FY2020 9,387.2. The FCF CAGRs are flattered by the FY2025 working-capital release and should not be read as trend growth. SBC is negligible (0.01-0.3% of revenue), so the SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs barely differ. Equity is attributable equity including perpetual bonds, as recorded in core_metrics.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +2% (H1 +3.7% YoY, but H2 container pricing weaker and US trailer duties bite); mid-single-digit growth as Enric/Raffles backlogs (Raffles US$5.09bn booked to 2030; Enric orders >RMB19bn) convert and the container fleet-replacement cycle normalises; fading to 2.5% (nominal CNY).
base.margin_rationale: Y1 6.6% = H1-2026 underlying EBITDA ~7.0% less ~0.4pp impairments; recovers to the ~7.5% mid-cycle (FY2019-25 ex-boom average ~8.0% gross of impairments) by Y5 and is held there - no boom year is capitalised.
base.capex_rationale: Y1 2.6% = FY2026 guided capex ~RMB3.45bn (2.2%) + ROU renewals; steady state 3.1% vs D&A 2.8% to fund ~3% growth.

scenario_narratives.base: The container segment spends 2026-27 working through price deflation (H1-2026 container net profit -81% on +2% volume) while the containership order book (~30% of fleet) caps new-box pricing; Enric's clean-energy equipment and Raffles' FPSO/FLNG backlog carry group growth at mid-single digits, CIMC Vehicles rebuilds around Global South and domestic demand as US China-to-US trailer exports are effectively closed by the 2026 AD/CVD orders, and FX losses fade as the RMB stabilises. Underlying EBITDA recovers from ~7.0% to its ~8% mid-cycle (7.5% net of impairments) by 2030 and stays there; no repeat of the 2021 boom is assumed.
scenario_narratives.bull: Red Sea/Hormuz route inefficiency and an ageing box fleet trigger a 2027-28 replacement upcycle like 2024's, lifting container volumes and price at the No.1 producer while Singamas retreats; Raffles' offshore-wind and FLNG yard is fully booked to 2030 at improving margins and Enric's LNG/hydrogen/green-methanol orders compound. Revenue grows 7-8% in 2027-28 and underlying EBITDA reaches ~9% gross (8.6% net) before settling at 8.2% - a mid-cycle above history because the mix has shifted toward energy/offshore equipment.
scenario_narratives.bear: Containership oversupply and 2026 freight-rate declines push shipping lines to defer box orders; new-container prices keep falling and COSCO's SULE takes share, revenue falls in 2026-27, and the finance/asset-management segment keeps losing ~RMB1.4bn/yr. US AD/CVD duties (CVD ~135%, AD ~131%) and transshipment enforcement shrink CIMC Vehicles' North American business, and repeated RMB-appreciation FX losses persist. Underlying EBITDA troughs near 6.6% gross (5.8% net) and only recovers to ~7% gross (6.5% net).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default): the container price cycle is still falling into H2-2026, US trailer duty orders are final, and the parent-level finance segment and FX losses have not yet turned. Base 50%: diversified segments and backlogs make a mid-cycle recovery the central path. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs a container replacement upcycle AND offshore/energy margin expansion together, two partly independent things going right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value CIMC on mid-cycle, not on the boom (FY2021/FY2024) or the trough (FY2025 attributable profit RMB136m to ordinary holders). Consolidated owner FCF is capitalised at a CNY WACC, then minority interests (book), perpetual bonds, leases and the declared dividend are deducted and associates/financial investments added, because ~27% of the group's book equity belongs to the minorities of five separately listed subsidiaries. Values are built in CNY and converted to HKD for the H-share quote; the A-share trades at a ~38% premium to the H-share on the same claim.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin: each 0.5pp of underlying EBITDA margin is worth roughly RMB0.8-1.0bn/yr of owner FCF on a ~RMB160bn revenue base - the dominant lever
Minority-interest leakage: if the profitable listed subsidiaries (Enric, Vehicles) keep capturing most of group profit, book NCI understates the minority claim
Associates (RMB10.3bn book) and the offshore-engineering asset pool may need further impairment
RMB/HKD and RMB/USD moves: FX losses hit the P&L, and the fx_rate bridge goes stale on price-only refreshes
Working capital swings of RMB5-8bn a year make any single year's reported FCF a poor anchor
SOE governance and H-share discount: value accrues equally to A and H holders, but the H-share has persistently traded 30-60% below the A-share
